findings.title: A sheet whose content changes creeps and oscillates for about 3 seconds instead of easing in 200 ms: `useSheetResize` feeds on its own animation.
findings.detail: `useSheetResize` (apps/web/src/frame/motion.ts) observes the sheet's scroll area with a ResizeObserver and, on every callback, calls `sheet.animate()` from the last measured height to the current one. The animation itself resizes the observed area, so the observer fires again on the next frame and starts another animation. After picking a category on a payment (list sheet, 732 px, then *From now on / Just this one*, 285 px) the sheet's height and top edge wander for about 3 s (1x CPU) with 135 `animate()` calls; on `main` it jumps once and rests within 154 ms. The run-1 fix made the hook attach (callback ref), which is what started the loop. The repo's test (`motion.spec` *a sheet whose content changes eases to its new height*) only asks for more than 3 distinct heights, so it passes (probe P2: the duration changed from 200 ms to 3000 ms and all seven motion tests stayed green). This is also the cause of the metrics flag `step:fix/4` (settle 1407 ms vs 579 on main) and plausibly part of `step:split-stuck/2` (a field error grows the sheet).

findings.title: The Home tab, tapped from a pushed screen in the first second after load, lands on More instead of Home (a regression from main), and the new Home-tab motion test fails about 1 run in 10 because of it.
findings.detail: `TabBar` remembers Home's history step in a module variable (`homeIndex`), set in an effect on every render where `active === 'home'`, from `history.location.state`. With the view transition, the router's history moves at once but React's new screen commits inside the transition's update callback, so a TabBar render with the old `active === 'home'` can run after the history already holds More's step; `homeIndex` becomes 1 (More). Home from Payments then calls `history.go(-1)` and lands on /more. Measured with a patched copy of my own build (a log line in that effect): `homeIndex=0 at / stateIdx=0`, then `pushState(/more)`, then `homeIndex=1 at /more stateIdx=1` 70-80 ms later, then at Home `go(-1) at /s/payments idx=2`, `popstate -> /more`. A second tap on Home then works. It needs the tap within about a second of load (0 of 20 failures with a 1.5 s settle), so a person meets it rarely; the test (`apps/web/e2e/motion.spec.ts` *the Home tab, tapped from a pushed screen deep in history*) meets it often because it taps straight after load, and it also made the `motion` suite fail unmutated in the sweep's breakage checks (6 mutants not judged until I re-ran them).
findings.repro: cd qa/e2e; N=30 ./node_modules/.bin/playwright test -c b05feel2.config.ts b05feel2-homeflake (BASE=http://localhost:4183 for a build of main); or cd apps/web && pnpm exec playwright test e2e/motion.spec.ts --project preview -g 'Home tab' --repeat-each 30 --workers 2

findings.title: The functional journey `own-transfer` fails intermittently on the branch (3 of 40) and never on main (0 of 40), with motion reduced; it failed in the sweep's full `pnpm e2e`.
findings.detail: `journeys.spec.ts` own-transfer, step 2 (*one row, filled in*): the scripted `covered` check reports the Public Bank → Ryt Bank row's button under `p.item-description "TransferFilled in"`: an element that is not inside the button that was tested, so a second copy of that row is on top at the moment of the check. This is the failure run 1 listed as finding 9 and marked fixed in `792e9fa`; it is still there. I did not find the cause: the page snapshot after a failure shows the Payments list with its usual sticky day header and one row, and the same steps repeated 160 times in my own contexts (1 and 4 parallel) never covered it. It is therefore a guess that something in the Payments list is briefly drawn twice while the search filter applies; nothing measured says what. The brief's *Done when* asks that functional e2e under reduced motion be reliable, and a 7% failure rate on one journey makes CI red at random.

findings.title: The push adds about 100 ms before the new screen's first frame at 4x CPU, and every tap with a screen change or a sheet step is flagged: 13 metrics flags (12 settle, 1 first change).
findings.detail: Brief §6: no transition delays a tap's first visible change past 100 ms. Measured at 4x CPU with the chunk warm, tap to the first frame that holds the new screen: head 175, 166, 144, 148, 124, 140 ms against main 66, 63, 55, 39, 36, 41 ms (qa/e2e/b05feel2-vtstart.spec.ts). The extra is the view transition's capture before it commits the new screen. `frame-times` with transitions: pushes hold 60 fps once moving (median 16.7 ms, 3-5% of frames over 33 ms), the start pause is 167-250 ms; tab crossfades drop more (10-19% of frames over 33 ms) in software compositing. The 12 settle flags are each a screen change or a sheet step that now takes the 200 ms of motion plus that pause (filmstrip email-setup/1: about 350 ms before the slide starts); `fix/4` and part of `split-stuck/2` are finding 1's sheet creep. I measured the first-frame delay and the start pause; I did not measure each flagged step on its own (payday/5, payday/8, proposal/3, claims/6, email-setup/4, capture-off/1, members/7 and /11, first-run/11), so for those the cause is the same shape, by reading the filmstrips, not by a measurement per step. Run 1's ledger (6) already accepts the tab crossfade as a lever for the owner.

findings.title: Rows that are a `<label>` around a checkbox lost their press feedback: no ripple, and the old tint was removed.
findings.detail: The ripple's `TAPPABLE` list takes `label[for]` but not a `label` without `for`. Three rows are labels around a control: *Who has paid you back* on a split (`shared/split.tsx`), the item picker of the Split sheet (`scan/split-sheets.tsx`, `MinePicker`) and *Change each quarter* (`outside/new-look.tsx`). B05 deleted `active:bg-accent` from the first two, so a tap on their text now shows nothing until the checkbox ticks. Brief §2: press feedback on everything tappable (list rows). My survey of every registered screen for `cursor: pointer` elements outside a ripple host found none, because these labels have the default cursor.

findings.title: Five guards in this slice survive a deliberate break, because no test holds them.
findings.detail: Phase-3 probes, each made alone and reverted: the ripple on a disabled control (P1), a sheet that animates for 3000 ms instead of 200 (P2, and see finding 1), a reject haptic while typing in a field (P3: the guard against buzzing per keystroke; also the `feel` unit suite stayed green), the router starting transitions without checking the browser can (P4: Chromium always can, so no test can see it; the fallback itself works, my R2-9 specs pass), and a skeleton that never fades into content (P5). Also unpinned: `hapticConstant`'s API-level mapping in Kotlin has no JVM test (the emulator test only checks that the answer holds `performed`, so swapping `REJECT` for `CONFIRM` would pass). Run-1's ten mutants were all killed again (17 of 23 in the sweep because the `motion` suite was red unmutated, finding 2; 6 of 6 on a re-run).
